title: TFA summer training institute combining supervised practice teaching, coaching, and coursework
description: The TFA training institute is a 5- to 7-week residential program in which corps members practice teaching in a real classroom under supervision while receiving observation, feedback, and coursework. The report describes how the institute "includes teaching summer school in a real classroom under the supervision of a regular classroom teacher", observation and feedback from TFA instructional coaches, small-group practice and reflection sessions, lesson planning clinics, and coursework in instructional planning, classroom management, diversity, and literacy development.
requirements: A residential training institute with summer school teaching placements, plus follow-up regional orientation of 1-2 weeks covering student achievement goals, lesson planning, data use, and relationship building
constraints: Training varies by region, though the report says it usually includes an induction, the institute, and a regional orientation
target_learners: novice teachers entering high-need public schools
examples: During training, corps members teach summer school typically for at least 2 hours per day and receive one-on-one coaching from TFA staff during their 2-year commitment
